Section 2 asserts a bound with no supporting hypothesis; with Setup as given (K compact, f continuous) the assertion is false (K={0}, f≡2 gives sup=2>1). This is not a case where proof omission is the problem — no proof of the stated claim could exist without an additional hypothesis, and none is supplied anywhere in the draft. Given that hypothesis, the proof is a one-liner: for all x, |f(x)| ≤ 1, so 1 is an upper bound of {|f(x)|}, hence sup ≤ 1; compactness/nonemptiness ensure the sup is finite and attained (max), though attainment isn't needed for the inequality. Also if "≤ 1" is meant sharp, note constant functions with |c| = 1 attain equality — Discussion's sharpness claim is fine but relies on such f being admissible, which again requires the normalization (and would be contradicted if f≡2 admissible). Also the claim as trivially true under hypothesis |f|≤1 makes the bound trivial — sup ≤ 1 follows immediately; the compactness hypothesis is unused for the bound (only for attainment). Omitting a proof of a one-line triviality is questionable in a math draft but not fatal once the hypothesis is present; but as stated, the omission masks the missing hypothesis.
